pr_title: Fix dhcpv4 renew/rebind intervals to match rfc2131
pr_body:
The current code calculates the renew and rebind intervals as 1/2 of t2-t1 or lifetime-t2, respectively, which is not what RFC 2131 mandates and results in networkd never attempting more than 2 renewals nor more than 2 rebinds, no matter how large the lease lifetime is.

These commits also add macros to make clear what the RFC describing the algorithms is, instead of using magic numbers.

Fixes #17909.
pr_comments: It seems that this makes `SD_DHCP_CLIENT_EVENT_TRANSIENT_FAILURE` event slightly delayed than previous. I have not reviewed this in detail, so I am not sure it is expected or not. But, at least the timeout in `test_dhcp_client_with_ipv4ll_without_dhcp_server` should be increased to make all CentOS CIs green.

> It seems that this makes `SD_DHCP_CLIENT_EVENT_TRANSIENT_FAILURE` event slightly delayed than previous. I have not reviewed this in detail, so I am not sure it is expected or not. But, at least the timeout in `test_dhcp_client_with_ipv4ll_without_dhcp_server` should be increased to make all CentOS CIs green.

it does slightly delay the transient failure event - i split that change out into its own commit, and i tried to add as much detail about behavior change to both commit messages.

In particular, the section 4.1 change that slightly delays the transient failure event is essentially only skipping the first 2-second timeout that the previous behavior was using; the RFC says 'start with 4 seconds' but our current code starts with 2, and the RFC also says the 4-second start is 'for example', so I think it should be fine to keep the existing behavior of starting at 2 seconds, if you think that's better. The rfc 'example' is for a 10Mbs network, so things are *definitely* faster nowdays.

for reference, from the rfc2131:
> For example, in a 10Mb/sec Ethernet
>    internetwork, the delay before the first retransmission SHOULD be 4
>    seconds randomized by the value of a uniform random number chosen
>    from the range -1 to +1.  Clients with clocks that provide resolution
>    granularity of less than one second may choose a non-integer
>    randomization value.  The delay before the next retransmission SHOULD
>    be 8 seconds randomized by the value of a uniform number chosen from
>    the range -1 to +1.  The retransmission delay SHOULD be doubled with
>    subsequent retransmissions up to a maximum of 64 seconds.
(only commenting about superficials here myself, I think @yuwata's take on all of this matters most)
@mrc0mmand Could you restart the two failed CentOS CI tests?
@mrc0mmand and @keszybz Thanks. All CentOS and Ubuntu CIs are green. Merging.

issue_context.title: networkd dhcpv4 client never attempts more than 2 renew and 2 rebind
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > git

**Used distribution**
 > Ubuntu

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > dhcpv4 client to follow RFC2131, performing more than 2 renew requests and more than 2 rebind requests

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > only 2 renew requests, and only 2 rebind requests

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 > configure an interface to use dhcpv4; acquire a dhcpv4 address, then stop the dhcpv4 server, and wait for the networkd client to perform its renewals and rebinds before expiring the lease

The current networkd dhcpv4 code appears to have a bug in its calculation of the t1 and t2 timeout, where the 'time_left' is always calculated as 1/2 of the total t1 or t2 time (respectively). However, RFC2131 specifies the 'time_left' should be 1/2 of the *remaining* time until the next phase, not 1/2 of the total time. Using 1/2 of the total time means there will only be 2 renewal requests, once at t1 and another at t1 + (t2 - t1) / 2. Then, a rebind request at t2, and one more at t2 + (expire - t2) / 2. Then the lease will expire.
